researchMethod: Phase 6 scale-out - filings fetched/extracted programmatically (research.js), analysis performed directly by Claude Code reading the extracted material, not by an automated LLM API call. Every factual claim below cites a specific source in the sources[] list.

quantContext.note: From this project's own scoring pipeline (companies.json + screener.js). Included for reference only - not itself a research source.

whyCheapBearCase.answer: TTD's discount is corroborated directly by the filings, not just by market sentiment. The stock has collapsed -42.5% over 3 months and -53.6% over 6 months [source: 1], and three cached headlines from the last two days ('Why Did TTD... Stocks Plummet To 52 Week Lows?', 'Why The Trade Desk (TTD) Shares Are Plunging Today', 'Trade Desk (TTD) Stock Is Falling Today') confirm this is an active, ongoing price decline, not stale news [source: 7, 8, 9]. The underlying fundamentals back up the bear case: after 18% revenue growth for full-year 2025 ($2,896.3M vs $2,444.8M in 2024) [source: 5], growth abruptly decelerated to just 3.0% year-over-year in Q2 2026 ($715.1M vs $694.0M in Q2 2025), with net income down 28.6% YoY ($64.4M vs $90.1M) and diluted EPS down 22.2% YoY ($0.14 vs $0.18) [source: 6]. Additionally, the company remains under active, unresolved shareholder litigation - a securities class action filed against it in February/March 2025 after an earlier stock-price drop, and separate Delaware Chancery Court litigation (the Gunderson and Scarantino actions) challenging its 2024 Nevada reincorporation, both still pending as of this 10-Q [source: 2, 3]. This is a real, filed growth-deceleration story with ongoing legal overhang, not simply a stock priced irrationally low.

revenueEpsTrend.answer: Deteriorating, and sharply so relative to the prior-year trend. Revenue grew only 3.0% YoY in Q2 2026 ($715.057M vs $694.039M in Q2 2025), a steep deceleration from the 18% YoY revenue growth reported for full-year 2025 [source: 5, 6]. Net income fell 28.6% YoY in Q2 2026 ($64.394M vs $90.129M), and diluted EPS fell 22.2% YoY ($0.14 vs $0.18) [source: 6]. For the six months ended June 30, computing H1 2025 by subtracting the reported Q3 2025 cumulative and quarterly XBRL figures (not a value directly stated in either filing's text, so flagged as derived): H1 2026 revenue of $1,403.9M was up only about 7.2% versus an implied H1 2025 figure of roughly $1,310.1M, while H1 2026 net income of $104.4M was down roughly 25.9% versus an implied H1 2025 figure of roughly $140.8M, and H1 2026 diluted EPS of $0.22 was down roughly 24% versus an implied H1 2025 figure of roughly $0.29 [source: 6]. Both the quarterly (directly reported) and the derived six-month figures point the same direction: growth is decelerating hard and profitability is contracting year-over-year.

marginTrend.answer: Compressing. Operating margin (income from operations / revenue) was 14.2% in Q2 2026 ($101.577M / $715.057M) versus 16.8% in Q2 2025 ($116.777M / $694.039M), a decline of about 2.6 percentage points [source: 6]. Using the same derived H1 2025 approach as above, H1 2026 operating margin was roughly 12.0% ($168.224M / $1,403.914M) versus a derived H1 2025 figure of roughly 13.1% ($171.229M / $1,310.060M), down about 1.1 points [source: 6]. This is a meaningfully worse margin trend than FY2025 as a whole, when operating margin actually expanded to 20% of revenue from 17% in 2024 [source: 5] - i.e., the margin-expansion story of 2025 has reversed in 2026.

guidanceChange.answer: Not determinable from available sources. The extracted 10-Q text does not contain an explicit forward-looking revenue or Adjusted EBITDA guidance figure, and the extraction pipeline's 'MD&A' text for this 10-Q actually captured risk-factor language rather than the quantitative results discussion (see sourcingNote), so no guidance commentary from that section was available either. The cached news headlines ('Why Did TTD... Stocks Plummet To 52 Week Lows?', 'Why The Trade Desk (TTD) Shares Are Plunging Today') were published August 10-11, 2026, close on the heels of the August 6, 2026 10-Q filing, which is suggestive of an earnings/guidance-related reaction, but only headline text was cached - article bodies were not fetched - so I cannot confirm whether a guidance cut specifically drove the decline versus the reported growth deceleration itself. I am not inferring the cause from the headlines alone.

catalysts.text: Continued investment in the Kokai platform and AI/machine-learning-driven value-added services and data, which management credited for higher utilization and pricing in FY2025 - if adoption reaccelerates, it could help offset the current growth slowdown.

OpenPath, the company's direct-to-publisher supply-chain initiative, is an ongoing investment area aimed at improving inventory quality and transparency versus real-time ad exchanges, a structural differentiator if it gains traction.

Active share repurchase program: an additional $350 million was authorized in February 2026, bringing total availability to $500 million, after the company already repurchased 26.2 million shares for $1.4 billion during 2025 - a real, ongoing capital-return mechanism.

risks.text: Confirmed, filed growth deceleration: revenue growth fell from 18% for full-year 2025 to just 3.0% year-over-year in Q2 2026, with net income down 28.6% and diluted EPS down 22.2% year-over-year in the same quarter - this is a real fundamental slowdown, not merely a market overreaction.

Ongoing, unresolved shareholder litigation: a securities class action filed in February/March 2025 following an earlier stock-price decline, plus separate Delaware Chancery Court litigation (Gunderson and Scarantino actions) challenging the company's 2024 reincorporation from Delaware to Nevada, both still active as of this 10-Q's filing date.

Structural client-concentration and lack of exclusivity, disclosed explicitly in the Risk Factors: the company has no exclusive relationships with advertising agencies or advertisers, clients can shift spend with limited notice, and two holding companies each represented more than 10% of gross billings for 2025 - meaning a single large client or holding-company decision could materially move revenue.

verdict.reasoning: The filing evidence leans toward 'value trap' rather than 'opportunity.' Unlike the EIX/UHS/ALL pilot names, where headline GAAP softness was traceable to one-time or accounting-timing items while underlying operating trends were flat-to-improving, TTD's Q2 2026 numbers show broad-based, genuine deterioration directly in the reported figures: revenue growth collapsed from 18% (FY2025) to 3.0% YoY, net income fell 28.6% YoY, diluted EPS fell 22.2% YoY, and operating margin compressed roughly 2.6 points YoY [source: 5, 6]. The stock's dramatic decline (-42.5% 3-month, -53.6% 6-month) [source: 1] and the very recent cached headlines confirming an active plunge to 52-week lows [source: 7, 8, 9] are consistent with the market correctly repricing a broken growth narrative rather than overreacting to noise. Two pieces of ongoing, unresolved litigation add further overhang [source: 2, 3]. Confidence is medium-high rather than high because guidance direction is genuinely not determinable from the sources available (no forward figures were extracted, and cached news is headline-only), and because a moderate P/E of 15.89 with still-positive ROE (17.22%) means this is not yet trading at obviously distressed levels - there is a real chance the deceleration proves temporary if the Kokai platform and OpenPath initiatives reaccelerate growth, which the filings alone cannot resolve.

sourcingNote: Two cached headlines were checked and excluded as not TTD-specific: 'Discover which S&P500 stocks are making waves on Monday' and 'Update: US Equity Indexes Mixed as Crude Oil, Treasury Yields Jump Amid Worsening Iran Geopolitics' (both general market roundups, ChartMill/Yahoo). A data-quality issue was also identified and is disclosed here: research.js's heading-based extraction pulled the same Risk Factors section text into both the 'mda' and 'riskFactors' fields for the 10-Q (and, to a lesser extent, the 10-K), rather than the quantitative Results of Operations discussion, likely because the 10-Q's document structure repeats risk-factor-style language near the MD&A heading. As a result, no directly-quoted MD&A narrative on Q2 2026 revenue/expense drivers was available; all quantitative trend analysis above was reconstructed from the XBRL companyfacts data (source 6) instead, with six-month 2025 comparison figures explicitly flagged as derived (subtracted from cumulative quarterly XBRL points) rather than directly stated in filing text.
